:::{#exm-logrank-test}
#### A log-rank test by hand

Group 1 has two participants, with events at times 1 and 2.
Group 2 has two participants, one with an event at time 3
and one censored at time 4.
The distinct failure times in the pooled data are
$t_1 = 1$, $t_2 = 2$, and $t_3 = 3$,
with the counts (@sec-logrank-notation)
in @tbl-logrank-hand.

:::{#tbl-logrank-hand}

| $i$ | $t_i$ | $r_{1i}$ | $r_{2i}$ | $r_i$ | $d_{1i}$ | $d_i$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 2 | 2 | 4 | 1 | 1 |
| 2 | 2 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 1 | 1 |
| 3 | 3 | 0 | 2 | 2 | 0 | 1 |

Risk-set and failure counts for the hand-computed log-rank test.
:::

Using group $g = 1$,
the observed count is $O_1 = 1 + 1 + 0 = 2$,
and the expected count (@eq-logrank-expected) is

$$
\ba
E_1
&= \sum_{i=1}^{3} \frac{r_{1i}}{r_i}\, d_i
&& \text{(sum of @eq-logrank-expected over failure times)}
\\
&= \frac{2}{4} \cdot 1 + \frac{1}{3} \cdot 1 + \frac{0}{2} \cdot 1
&& \text{(substitute counts from @tbl-logrank-hand)}
\\
&= \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3} + 0
&& \text{(arithmetic)}
\\
&= \frac{5}{6},
&& \text{(common denominator 6)}
\ea
$$

so $O_1 - E_1 = 2 - 5/6 = 7/6$.
The variance estimate (@eq-logrank-var-2grp) is

$$
\ba
\widehat{\Varf{O_1 - E_1}}
&= \sum_{i=1}^{3}
   \frac{r_{1i}\, r_{2i}\, d_i\, (r_i - d_i)}{r_i^2\,(r_i - 1)}
&& \text{(@eq-logrank-var-2grp)}
\\
&= \frac{2 \cdot 2 \cdot 1 \cdot 3}{4^2 \cdot 3}
 + \frac{1 \cdot 2 \cdot 1 \cdot 2}{3^2 \cdot 2}
 + \frac{0 \cdot 2 \cdot 1 \cdot 1}{2^2 \cdot 1}
&& \text{(substitute counts from @tbl-logrank-hand)}
\\
&= \frac{12}{48} + \frac{4}{18} + 0
&& \text{(arithmetic)}
\\
&= \frac{1}{4} + \frac{2}{9}
&& \text{(reduce fractions)}
\\
&= \frac{17}{36}.
&& \text{(common denominator 36)}
\ea
$$

The log-rank statistic (@eq-logrank-stat-2grp) is then

$$
\ba
\chi^2_{\text{LR}}
&= \frac{(O_1 - E_1)^2}{\widehat{\Varf{O_1 - E_1}}}
&& \text{(@eq-logrank-stat-2grp)}
\\
&= \frac{(7/6)^2}{17/36}
&& \text{(substitute)}
\\
&= \frac{49/36}{17/36}
&& \text{(square the numerator)}
\\
&= \frac{49}{17}
&& \text{(cancel the common factor $1/36$)}
\\
&\approx 2.88.
&& \text{(arithmetic)}
\ea
$$

The $0.95$ quantile of $\chi^2_1$ is approximately $3.84$,
and $2.88 < 3.84$,
so the log-rank test (@def-logrank-test) does not reject $H_0$ at $\alpha = 0.05$
(the p-value is approximately $0.09$).
With only four participants, the large-sample $\chi^2_1$ approximation is rough;
this example only illustrates the arithmetic.
:::
